scope: The scripture as first printed and as revised: the Book of Mormon in the first edition (Palmyra, 1830) and the third, 'carefully revised by the translator' (Nauvoo, 1840); the revelations in the Book of Commandments (Zion, 1833), left unfinished when a mob destroyed the press, and in the Doctrine and Covenants of 1835 (Kirtland, with the Lectures on Faith) and 1845 (Nauvoo, the edition that announces the martyrdom). Then the succession itself: the Times and Seasons of September 1844, with the epistle of the Twelve and the trial of Sidney Rigdon, and James J. Strang's counter-claim from Voree, the Voree Herald of 1846 and The Diamond of 1848, with the letter of 18 June 1844 on which it rests. The 1837 Kirtland edition of the Book of Mormon was not found in an open scan: QUEUED. Strang's Book of the Law of the Lord (1851; 1856), the RLDS editions (from 1874; the Authorized Version of 1908) and the Pearl of Great Price (1851): QUEUED. Manuscripts held by the Joseph Smith Papers are under that project's terms and are not seated.

why_seated: Asked for as the Book of Mormon, and seated only beside the other traditions that divided in the same years: in 1844 Joseph Smith was killed at Carthage (27 June) and the church he founded split over who should lead it, in the same months that the Bab declared his mission in Shiraz (22–23 May) and the Millerites waited for 22 October.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 27 October 2026: "need to seat the book of mormon but im not doing it without several diverging simultaneous traditions in the batch" — offered the traditions that divided in 1844 (the Latter Day Saint succession, the Bab's declaration, the Millerite disappointment, the Taiping beginnings), or the Book of Mormon's own editions — "1. definitely. lets go."
